_source: Deterministic parse of raw Telair PBX CSV exports (ExportCallRecords, InboundCalls_Detailed, CallQueue_Detailed per queue) via scripts/parse_call_logs.py, chained against assets/data/reports/2026-10-16/call-logs.json. Replaces this date's earlier PDF-text-extraction of this same file (committed under this date previously) now that the raw CSVs are available. Report's cover is misdated — true date is 2026-10-19 (Monday); see tasks.json's own _source note. Core figures close to Daily Operations Report - 20th October 2026.pdf but with a handful of verbatim-recorded gaps this date — see _summaryVsGrandTotalNote, _staffCountNote and _outboundTenDayTrendNote.
_summaryVsGrandTotalNote: This file's own summary (from the deduplicated InboundCalls_Detailed file: 358 total/295 accepted/63 missed) reads 1 OVER the PDF's own pie chart (357 total/294 accepted/63 missed, 82%/18% — identical percentages). The extra accepted call traces to David Antioch: this file's raw-CSV-derived inboundByStaff shows him with 72 calls/115 min, versus 71 calls/113 min on the PDF's own printed Inbound Calls - All Staff table — every other one of the 10 names matches exactly, and excluding the 1-call difference, the remaining total matches the PDF's pie exactly (294). The queue-level grandTotal (from the four named queues) sums to 292 accepted/63 missed (355 total) — 2 short of the PDF's own pie, the same kind of pre-existing PDF-internal inconsistency seen on prior dates (its own chart doesn't equal its own queue-breakdown sum), not introduced here. All figures recorded verbatim rather than reconciled to agree.
_tenDayTrendNote: accepted/missed/answerRatePct/overallAvgWaitSec all chain-matched 2026-10-16's own committed-equivalent trend exactly at positions 0-8; position 9 is this date's own raw-CSV-derived figure (295 accepted, 63 missed, 82% answer rate, 45 sec overall average wait) — answerRatePct/overallAvgWaitSec at position 9 also match the PDF's own printed chart values exactly (82%, 45 sec). FLAG FOR USER REVIEW: this report's own printed 'Overall Average Wait Time - 10 Day Trends' chart shows a different, much lower value for the oldest point on its own chart (Tue 06-Oct), printing 45 sec there versus the 123 sec chain-carried above (which traces back through every committed date since it was first recorded). Positions 1-7 on that same printed chart otherwise match this chain closely (one point, Tue 13-Oct, differs by 1 sec: 45 printed vs 44 chained). Recorded verbatim per policy, not reconciled — the chain-verified figure (123) is kept here since the source PDF offers no way to tell which value is authoritative for that historical date, and the same single-point divergence recurs independently across every per-queue wait-time chart on this date's own report (see _queuesNote).
_queuesNote: accepted/missed for all four queues chain-match 2026-10-16's own committed-equivalent data exactly at positions 0-8, and all three non-zero queues' accepted/missed/avgWaitSec at position 9 match the PDF's own queue breakdown and per-queue 10-day charts exactly (Appointments 186/25, 40 sec; General Enquiries 105/38, 54 sec; Canberra Vasectomy 1/0, 41 sec) — clean match, no queue-level gap this date. FLAG FOR USER REVIEW: as with the top-level overallAvgWaitSec trend, this report's own printed four-panel 'Queue Average Wait Time - 10 Day Trends' chart shows a different, much lower value at its own oldest point (Tue 06-Oct) for every non-zero queue — Appointments 33 printed vs 110 chained, General Enquiries 56 printed vs 151 chained, Canberra Vasectomy 35 printed vs 86 chained — while every other position matches closely (occasional ±1-2 sec rounding noise). Recorded verbatim, not reconciled; this reads as a genuine, one-off revision of that single historical data point across every wait-time chart in this report, not a parsing error on our part, and not something the raw CSVs (long since rotated out of OneDrive for that date) can settle either way.
_patientServiceKpiNote: longestCallDurationSec/longestCallAt/longestCallAgent and longestWaitingTimeSec/longestWaitingAt all match the PDF's own Patient Service KPI panel exactly (613 sec at 4:34 PM by Pinky De Paz; 749 sec at 10:59 AM, attributed via the Longest Wait Per Queue table to Jasmine Deery in General Enquiries). avgCallHandlingSec (146) matches the PDF's own printed figure exactly.
_staffCountNote: 9 of inboundByStaff's 10 names match the PDF's own printed Inbound Calls - All Staff table exactly on both calls and duration. The tenth, David Antioch, shows 72 calls/115 min here versus 71 calls/113 min on the PDF — a 1-call/2-min gap not seen on the other 9 names (see _summaryVsGrandTotalNote for how this flows through to the file's own summary).
_outboundDurationNote: outboundByStaff's own call counts match the PDF's own 9-name outbound staff table exactly for every name (32/17/14/12/11/7/6/5/2, summing to the confirmed 106-call total, which also matches this file's own summary.totalOutbound and the PDF's own 'Total Outbound Calls = 106 Calls' header exactly, in both the full and short PDF versions). Several per-agent durationMins values differ from the PDF's own printed minutes (e.g. Shae Connors 96 here vs 80 printed, Ambrosie Brassil 28 vs 35, Jasmine Deery 17 vs 19), while others match exactly — consistent with each source rounding individual call durations to the nearest minute before summing in a slightly different way, not a data error; recorded verbatim rather than adjusted to match.
_outboundTenDayTrendNote: Chain-matches 2026-10-16's own committed-equivalent trend exactly at positions 0-8 (this field covers ALL outbound extensions — reception + other — not just the reception-staff subset in outboundByStaff: 106 reception + 113 other = 219). FLAG FOR USER REVIEW (sixth consecutive date): this report's own 'Outbound 10 Day Trend Reporting' chart does not print 219 for today — it continues the same persistent divergence from the chain-verified/raw-CSV-derived totals first flagged on 2026-10-13, now fully explained: the PDF's own chart appears to track only reception-extension outbound calls (close to the 106 in summary.totalOutbound) rather than the full all-extensions total computed here. Both figures are genuine — they're just measuring different things — but since the chart's own label doesn't make that scope clear, and earlier dates' PDF-printed values were recorded as a straight divergence rather than resolved, this file continues to carry the full all-extensions total per the established chain, with this note now documenting the likely explanation for the user's awareness.
